items.transcript: When the sponsor pulled out I cut the second weekend instead of cutting vendor spots, because the vendors had already paid for stock and the team agreed.
I went to the vendor first because their deadline was the earliest.
I picked the second option. It looked fine.
I let the team vote rather than assigning roles myself, because people who choose their job stick with it. It cost us a day, but nobody checked out.
I did the whole budget myself so it would be done faster.
I told everyone the same day so nobody heard it secondhand, and I explained what we were keeping instead of what we lost.
Once the budget dropped I switched to the smaller venue instead of keeping the hall, since the hall would have eaten everything and the volunteers would have had nothing to work with.
I kept the plan exactly as it was. I liked the plan.
The chart showed sales were flat in the north but growing in the west, so I moved the budget west rather than spreading it evenly, because that is where the trend actually was.
I asked around the office before deciding, because nobody had told me why the client was unhappy. I found out their old vendor had missed two deadlines.
I called the volunteer who was upset before the meeting, because I did not want her to hear about the cut in front of everyone. It slowed us down but she stayed.
After the first launch failed I tried again the next week since we had learned what broke.
